capabilities.target: external enrichment API drawing on the shared monthly quota
sub-agent researcher instance investigating an account
CRM account fields: industry, size, headquarters

inputs.source: Nightly batch of CRM account rows (40,000 rows/night)

instructions.note: "Keep going until every row is complete" sets no limit on retries, lookups, or spawned sub agents. Roughly 3 percent of the 40,000-row batch (about 1,200 rows) has malformed company names that never return a complete result, so this instruction guarantees sustained retrying and spawning every run.
"retry, or spawn a researcher sub agent" leaves the retry-versus-spawn decision, and the depth or count of any spawning, entirely to model judgment with no stated stopping criteria.

Sales and marketing tools dependent on the same enrichment quota

controls.name: Per-run and per-day spend cap on enrich.lookup
Maximum retries per row and maximum sub-agent spawn depth/count
Dedicated enrichment API key/quota isolated from sales and marketing
Real-time spend/quota alert with automatic halt
Dead-letter handling for rows that fail after N attempts
Human approval gate before spawning researcher sub-agents beyond a low default

findings.title: Unbounded spend loop against shared enrichment quota (TC6) with no caps or alerts

attack_path.note: Nightly batch of 40,000 account rows, ~3 percent with malformed company names that never return a complete result
Billed-per-call lookup invoked per row and retried indefinitely on failure or incomplete result per prompt.md:2-3
Each call draws on the enrichment API quota shared with sales and marketing
Quota exhaustion before month end breaks sales and marketing tools that depend on the same key

forecast.watch_signal: Monthly quota consumption rate versus days elapsed; nightly spend per batch trending upward as batch size or malformed-row rate grows.

evidence.observation: enrich.lookup is billed per call against an API key and monthly quota shared with sales and marketing; when the quota runs out, their tools stop working until the next month.
There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents, and no spend alert on the enrichment account.

"Keep going until every row is complete," while roughly 3 percent of the 40,000-row batch (about 1,200 rows) has malformed company names that never return a complete result, so the loop has no natural stopping point.

recommendations.action: Enforce a hard per-run and per-day spend cap on enrich.lookup, enforced outside the model, that halts further calls once reached.
Issue the enrichment agent its own dedicated API key and quota, isolated from sales and marketing tools, so exhausting it cannot disrupt other teams.
Add real-time spend and quota-consumption alerting with an automatic halt when a threshold is crossed, independent of the model.
Cap retries per row and route rows that fail after N attempts to a dead-letter list for human review instead of retrying indefinitely.

findings.title: Unbounded recursive sub-agent spawning with no depth or count limit

attack_path.note: Rows with incomplete or failed lookups trigger the spawn branch per prompt.md:2-3
Sub agent spawned to investigate the account; sub agents can themselves spawn further researchers with no stated depth or count limit
Each spawned researcher can continue to call the billed lookup
Recursive spawning multiplies quota consumption with no bound

forecast.watch_signal: Count and depth of concurrently active researcher sub-agents per batch run.

evidence.observation: Sub agents can spawn their own researchers, and there is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents.
"retry, or spawn a researcher sub agent to investigate the account" gives the model discretion to spawn with no stated limit on depth or count.

recommendations.action: Enforce a hard maximum on sub-agent spawn depth and total researcher sub-agents created per batch run, enforced by the orchestrator rather than the prompt.
Require human approval, with raw action visibility, before spawning a researcher sub-agent beyond a low default count.
Log and alert on active sub-agent count and spawn chain depth per run.

rating.rationale: Both findings reach critical inherent and residual risk: an internal nightly batch feeds a billed, shared-quota lookup (S3, spend action) and an unbounded recursive sub-agent spawn capability (S3, delegate action), under full autonomy (A4) with no step, retry, spawn, spend, or depth limits, no spend alerting, and no dedicated quota isolation from sales and marketing. About 3 percent of the 40,000-row nightly batch (roughly 1,200 rows) can never produce a complete result, so the instruction to 'keep going until every row is complete' guarantees sustained retries and spawning on every run, not merely a possible exploitation path. No declared control covers either path, so residual equals the inherent floor for both findings. Forecasts stay critical under longer task horizon, data scope expansion, and control removal triggers because there are no existing controls left to decay; the same fixes close both the present and projected risk: a hard spend cap, a dedicated quota, a bounded retry/spawn depth, and a dead-letter path for unresolvable rows.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No MCP config, tool manifest, or IaC was provided; capability details such as sub-agent credential inheritance and whether crm_write is gated are inferred rather than confirmed, so some fields (e.g., credential_scope: unknown) reflect that gap.
Cost and operational figures (40,000 rows, ~3 percent malformed) are taken as given in the runtime notes and not independently verified.
